We have previously reported on multiple stories about Apple Vision Pro applications in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced that it has completed the first surgical procedure using a new Vision Pro application.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy, utilising the SportSuite Vision application. The application can bring "critical digital content into the surgeon's spatial environment," including arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images.

Below is Stryker's description of the application:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's field of view, allowing them to simultaneously see physical objects and digital tools in the operating room, including arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images. During arthroscopic surgery, surgeons typically rely on multiple displays in the operating room to view imaging and surgical data. By integrating multiple data sources into the surgeon's line of sight, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional monitors and support a more streamlined, ergonomically optimised surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorisation on 17 July. According to Stryker, this is the first application authorised by the FDA for use with Vision Pro during surgical procedures.
